We reviewed root cause hypotheses (burst routing + client retry behavior + backend batching), quick mitigations (adjust client timeouts, exponential backoff, increase request queue depth), and next steps: share logs, run targeted load test, and start a Dedicated capacity trial to validate stability.

Dedicated vs hosted routing for spike resilience
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-05-02
Start: 10:00 AM UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Emma Li (Redwood AE), Raj Patel (Redwood SE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Alice Chen (FinServe CTO), Ben Martinez (FinServe SRE), Priya Singh (Product), Liam O'Connor (QA)

Summary: quick follow-up on last week's incident; go over logs, verify mitigations, align on next steps for POC stability.

[00:00] Emma Li: Hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. Quick check, is this audio ok?
[00:08] Alice Chen: Yep, all good. So we had the spike last Friday around 14:22 local, saw a bunch of 502/504s and timeouts from our app side.
[00:18] Ben Martinez: And to add, our client retried aggressively which seemed to amplify the load, we saw a cascading effect.
[00:26] Raj Patel: Yeah, based on initial metrics from the platform we saw concurrent request growth and a KV cache pressure increase which bumped tail latency and then some internal worker restarts.
[00:38] Priya Singh: Can you explain KV cache pressure? sounds like the cache was being evicted?
[00:44] Raj Patel: Right, so the runtime's prefix/KV cache stores context for ongoing sessions — when a lot of unique sessions came in, the cache footprint spiked and memory got tighter, leading to slightly longer GC pauses and then increased request queuing.
[00:58] Emma Li: There might be transcription of product names wrong in the logs, but the sequence was: spike -> queueing -> a few 5xxs -> client retries -> more load.
[01:12] Ben Martinez: From our side, our LB timeout was 30s and the client lib retries after 5s and then 10s — it basically retried into the degraded window.
[01:22] Raj Patel: Exactly, retry storms are classic. Two immediate fixes we pushed to many customers: implement exponential backoff on client retries and a jitter, and reduce client-side max retry count.
[01:34] Alice Chen: Any changes on the server side we should apply now?
[01:38] Raj Patel: Short term: raise worker pool size slightly, increase queue depth, and set a circuit breaker that fails fast when error rate > X% for Y seconds. Also tune the load-balancer idle timeout — we've seen some LBs cut connections too early causing upstream errors.
[01:56] Liam O'Connor: Are there config examples you can send for NGINX or ALB?
[01:59] Emma Li: Yes, Raj will share a small doc with NGINX timeout and proxy settings — those helped another customer.
[02:06] Ben Martinez: We also saw a few 5xxs referencing model worker restarts. Is that because of OOM or a process crash?
[02:12] Raj Patel: Logs show worker restarts coinciding with the cache pressure spike; not a model crash per se, more like the runtime evicting sessions and reinitializing workers. We're collecting finer-grained heap and GC metrics in the incident bundle.
[02:26] Alice Chen: Would Dedicated capacity avoid this? we were thinking a dedicated pool might mean more predictable throughput.
[02:30] Raj Patel: Dedicated helps with noisy-neighbor issues and gives predictable concurrency. For spike resilience you'd also want autoscaling policies tuned (fast scale-up thresholds) and warm standby slots. Dedicated doesn't eliminate bad client-side retries though.
[02:46] Priya Singh: Any quick wins for us to do before the Dedicated trial?
[02:49] Emma Li: Yes — implement exponential backoff, drop to single retry for short requests, instrument and send us the synthetic spike results. Also add a short-circuit in the client to treat 5xxs as transient but back off aggressively.
[03:04] Ben Martinez: We'll change the client lib and run a 2 hour test with ramp and spikes.
[03:08] Raj Patel: We'll also share a trimmed log bundle that shows the incident timeline, and a suggested HPA/autoscale profile and queue/backpressure settings.
[03:17] Alice Chen: On observability — can you add a per-route alert for 5xx rate + queue depth? we want to be alerted before users notice.
[03:23] Marco Ruiz: Yes, Redwood Console can emit an alert for 5xx rate > 1% for 2 minutes, and for queue depth > threshold; we'll add the runbook steps into the alert.
[03:34] Liam O'Connor: Security question — did anything touch PII? we need confirmation for compliance.
[03:38] Emma Li: No PII was exposed; requests were user prompts only. We'll include a note in the incident bundle and link to the audit logs showing access.
[03:47] Ben Martinez: Also curious about retry headers — are you suggesting a Retry-After or custom header so we can coordinate client behavior?
[03:53] Raj Patel: We can emit a Retry-After and a rate-limit style header for longer-running requests; that's on the roadmap and can be simulated in the Dedicated trial.
[04:01] Alice Chen: Ok, timeline and owners?
[04:04] Emma Li: Raj will send config examples and the log bundle by Monday 2026-05-03; Ben will run the synthetic test by 2026-05-06; Marco will draft the Dedicated trial plan by 2026-05-05. We'll reconvene after the load test — propose 2026-05-10 for a results review.
[04:20] Priya Singh: Sounds good. Also, one more ask: can you provide guidance on quantization or model variant switching if workers are overloaded?
[04:28] Raj Patel: Short answer: you can fail over to a cheaper/less memory-intense variant as a fallback — Redwood supports model routing rules. We'll include recommended variants for your prompt lengths in the doc.
[04:38] Ben Martinez: Any immediate client timeout settings you'd recommend?
[04:41] Raj Patel: Keep client request timeout shorter than LB idle timeout, use 5s initial retry with exponential backoff and jitter, limit to 2 retries for interactive flows. For long-running batches, use async job patterns.
[04:55] Emma Li: Great. We'll share the incident bundle and configs, and set up the Dedicated trial paperwork. Thanks everyone.
[05:02] Alice Chen: Thanks, appreciate it.

End of transcript.
